statement: (A q : ℕ) (hA : 0 < A) (hq : 0 < q) : ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p → ((p ∣ A ∧ Nat.gcd p q = 1) ↔ (p ∣ A ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ q → ¬(r ∣ p)))

theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_423907_0_gs2_f0_gs1 (A q : ℕ) (hA : 0 < A) (hq : 0 < q) :
  ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p →
    ((p ∣ A ∧ Nat.gcd p q = 1) ↔
     (p ∣ A ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ q → ¬(r ∣ p))) := by
  intro p hp
  have h_imp : (p ∣ A ∧ Nat.gcd p q = 1) → (p ∣ A ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ q → ¬(r ∣ p)) := by
    intro h
    have h₁ : p ∣ A := h.1
    have h₂ : Nat.gcd p q = 1 := h.2
    have h₃ : ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ q → ¬(r ∣ p) := by
      intro r h₄ h₅
      have h₆ : ¬(r ∣ p) := by
        by_contra h₇
        have h₈ : r ∣ p := by tauto
        have h₉ : r ∣ Nat.gcd p q := Nat.dvd_gcd h₈ h₅
        have h₁₀ : r ∣ 1 := by simpa [h₂] using h₉
        have h₁₁ : r = 1 := Nat.le_antisymm (Nat.le_of_dvd (by norm_num) h₁₀) (Nat.Prime.one_lt h₄ |>.le)
        have h₁₂ := Nat.Prime.ne_one h₄
        contradiction
      exact h₆
    exact ⟨h₁, h₃⟩

  have h_converse : (p ∣ A ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ q → ¬(r ∣ p)) → (p ∣ A ∧ Nat.gcd p q = 1) := by
    intro h
    have h₁ : p ∣ A := h.1
    have h₂ : ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ q → ¬(r ∣ p) := h.2
    have h₃ : Nat.gcd p q = 1 := by
      by_contra h₄
      -- Assume the gcd is not 1 and derive a contradiction
      have h₅ : Nat.gcd p q ≠ 1 := h₄
      have h₆ : Nat.gcd p q > 1 := by
        have h₇ : Nat.gcd p q ≠ 0 := by
          by_contra h₇
          have h₈ : Nat.gcd p q = 0 := by simpa using h₇
          have h₉ : p = 0 := by
            have h₁₀ : Nat.gcd p q ∣ p := Nat.gcd_dvd_left p q
            have h₁₁ : Nat.gcd p q = 0 := h₈
            have h₁₂ : 0 ∣ p := by simpa [h₁₁] using h₁₀
            simpa using h₁₂
          omega
        have h₈ : Nat.gcd p q ≥ 2 := by
          by_contra h₉
          have h₁₀ : Nat.gcd p q ≤ 1 := by omega
          have h₁₁ : Nat.gcd p q = 1 := by
            interval_cases Nat.gcd p q <;> simp_all (config := {decide := true})
          contradiction
        omega
      -- There exists a prime r dividing the gcd
      have h₇ : ∃ r, Nat.Prime r ∧ r ∣ Nat.gcd p q := by
        have h₈ : Nat.gcd p q > 1 := h₆
        exact Nat.exists_prime_and_dvd (by omega)
      obtain ⟨r, hr, h₉⟩ := h₇
      have h₁₀ : r ∣ p := by
        have h₁₁ : r ∣ Nat.gcd p q := h₉
        have h₁₂ : Nat.gcd p q ∣ p := Nat.gcd_dvd_left p q
        exact dvd_trans h₁₁ h₁₂
      have h₁₁ : r ∣ q := by
        have h₁₂ : r ∣ Nat.gcd p q := h₉
        have h₁₃ : Nat.gcd p q ∣ q := Nat.gcd_dvd_right p q
        exact dvd_trans h₁₂ h₁₃
      have h₁₂ : ¬(r ∣ p) := h₂ r hr h₁₁
      exact h₁₂ h₁₀
    exact ⟨h₁, h₃⟩

  have h_main : ((p ∣ A ∧ Nat.gcd p q = 1) ↔ (p ∣ A ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ q → ¬(r ∣ p))) := by
    constructor
    · -- Prove the forward direction: (p ∣ A ∧ Nat.gcd p q = 1) → (p ∣ A ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ q → ¬(r ∣ p))
      intro h
      exact h_imp h
    · -- Prove the backward direction: (p ∣ A ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, Nat.Prime r → r ∣ q → ¬(r ∣ p)) → (p ∣ A ∧ Nat.gcd p q = 1)
      intro h
      exact h_converse h

  exact h_main

statement: (G : Type*) [Group G] (x : G) (hx : x ^ 2 = 1) : (x ≠ 1) ↔ Nat.Prime (orderOf x)

theorem xgv2_exercise_10_1_16_ (G : Type*) [Group G]
   (x : G) (hx : x ^ 2 = 1) :   (x ≠ 1) ↔   Nat.Prime (orderOf x) := by
  have h₁ : orderOf x ∣ 2 := by
    have h₂ : x ^ 2 = 1 := hx
    have h₃ : orderOf x ∣ 2 := by
      -- Use the fact that `orderOf x` divides any integer `n` such that `x^n = 1`
      have h₄ : x ^ 2 = 1 := h₂
      have h₅ : orderOf x ∣ 2 := by
        apply orderOf_dvd_of_pow_eq_one
        simpa using h₄
      exact h₅
    exact h₃

  have h₂ : orderOf x = 1 ∨ orderOf x = 2 := by
    have h₃ : orderOf x ∣ 2 := h₁
    have h₄ : orderOf x = 1 ∨ orderOf x = 2 := by
      have h₅ : orderOf x ∣ 2 := h₃
      have h₆ : orderOf x ≤ 2 := Nat.le_of_dvd (by decide) h₅
      have h₇ : orderOf x ≥ 1 := by
        apply Nat.pos_of_ne_zero
        intro h
        have h₈ : orderOf x = 0 := by simpa using h
        have h₉ : x ^ orderOf x = 1 := by
          simp [orderOf_eq_zero_iff] at h₈ ⊢ <;> aesop
        simp_all [orderOf_eq_zero_iff]
        <;> aesop
      interval_cases orderOf x <;> norm_num at h₅ ⊢ <;> aesop
    exact h₄

  have h₃ : x = 1 ↔ orderOf x = 1 := by
    constructor
    · intro h
      rw [h]
      simp
    · intro h
      have h₄ : x ^ orderOf x = 1 := by
        exact pow_orderOf_eq_one x
      have h₅ : orderOf x = 1 := h
      have h₆ : x ^ 1 = 1 := by
        rw [h₅] at h₄
        simpa using h₄
      simpa using h₆

  have h₄ : (x ≠ 1) ↔ (orderOf x = 2) := by
    constructor
    · -- Prove the forward direction: if x ≠ 1, then orderOf x = 2
      intro h
      have h₅ : orderOf x = 1 ∨ orderOf x = 2 := h₂
      cases h₅ with
      | inl h₅ =>
        -- If orderOf x = 1, then x = 1, which contradicts x ≠ 1
        have h₆ : x = 1 := by
          have h₇ : x ^ orderOf x = 1 := pow_orderOf_eq_one x
          have h₈ : orderOf x = 1 := h₅
          rw [h₈] at h₇
          simpa using h₇
        contradiction
      | inr h₅ =>
        -- If orderOf x = 2, then we are done
        exact h₅
    · -- Prove the backward direction: if orderOf x = 2, then x ≠ 1
      intro h
      have h₅ : orderOf x = 2 := h
      have h₆ : x ≠ 1 := by
        by_contra h₇
        have h₈ : x = 1 := h₇
        have h₉ : orderOf x = 1 := by
          rw [h₈]
          simp
        rw [h₅] at h₉
        norm_num at h₉
      exact h₆

  have h₅ : Nat.Prime (orderOf x) ↔ (orderOf x = 2) := by
    constructor
    · -- Prove the forward direction: if Nat.Prime (orderOf x), then orderOf x = 2
      intro h
      have h₆ : orderOf x = 1 ∨ orderOf x = 2 := h₂
      cases h₆ with
      | inl h₆ =>
        -- If orderOf x = 1, then Nat.Prime (orderOf x) is false, which contradicts h
        have h₇ : ¬Nat.Prime (orderOf x) := by
          rw [h₆]
          norm_num [Nat.Prime]
        contradiction
      | inr h₆ =>
        -- If orderOf x = 2, then we are done
        exact h₆
    · -- Prove the backward direction: if orderOf x = 2, then Nat.Prime (orderOf x)
      intro h
      have h₆ : orderOf x = 2 := h
      rw [h₆]
      <;> decide

  have h₆ : (x ≠ 1) ↔ Nat.Prime (orderOf x) := by
    rw [h₄]
    rw [h₅]
    <;> aesop

  exact h₆

theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_295027_0_gs0 (a b : ℤ) (ha : a > 1) (hb : b > 1)

      rw [← pow_mul]
      <;> ring_nf

    -- We need to show that b^n - 1 divides b^(k * n) - 1
    have h₃ : (b ^ n - 1 : ℤ) ∣ (b ^ (k * n) - 1 : ℤ) := by
      -- Use the fact that b^(k * n) - 1 = (b^n)^k - 1 and factor it
      have h₄ : (b ^ (k * n) - 1 : ℤ) = (b ^ n) ^ k - 1 := by
        rw [show (k * n : ℕ) = n * k by ring]
        rw [show (b : ℤ) ^ (n * k : ℕ) = (b ^ n : ℤ) ^ k by
          rw [← pow_mul]
          <;> ring_nf
        ]
        <;> ring_nf
      rw [h₄]
      -- Use the difference of powers factorization to show divisibility
      have h₅ : (b ^ n - 1 : ℤ) ∣ ((b ^ n : ℤ) ^ k - 1 : ℤ) := by
        -- Use the fact that x - 1 divides x^k - 1 for any integer x
        simpa only [one_pow] using sub_dvd_pow_sub_pow (b ^ n) 1 k
      exact h₅
    exact h₃
  exact h_main

theorem lean_workbook_plus_43801 (a b : ℤ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) : gcd a b ∣ lcm a b   := by

  To prove that for any nonzero integers \(a\) and \(b\), the greatest common divisor (gcd) of \(a\) and \(b\) divides the least common multiple (lcm) of \(a\) and \(b\), we can use the property that the gcd of two numbers divides their lcm. theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_376643_3_gs2 (a b : ℤ)
  (ha : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → ∃ y : ℤ, y^2 ≡ a [ZMOD p])
  (hb : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → ∃ y : ℤ, y^2 ≡ b [ZMOD p]) :
  ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → ∃ y : ℤ, y^2 ≡ a * b [ZMOD p] := by
  have h_main : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → ∃ y : ℤ, y^2 ≡ a * b [ZMOD p] := by
    intro p hp
    -- Use the fact that a and b are quadratic residues modulo p to find integers x and y such that x^2 ≡ a (mod p) and y^2 ≡ b (mod p).
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := ha p hp
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hb p hp
    -- Consider the product (xy)^2 = x^2 * y^2.
    use x * y
    -- Simplify the congruence (x * y)^2 ≡ a * b (mod p).
    have h1 : (x * y : ℤ) ^ 2 ≡ a * b [ZMOD p] := by
      calc
        (x * y : ℤ) ^ 2 = x ^ 2 * y ^ 2 := by ring
        _ ≡ a * b [ZMOD p] := by
          -- Use the given congruences x^2 ≡ a (mod p) and y^2 ≡ b (mod p).
          have h2 : x ^ 2 ≡ a [ZMOD p] := hx
          have h3 : y ^ 2 ≡ b [ZMOD p] := hy
          have h4 : (x ^ 2 : ℤ) * y ^ 2 ≡ a * b [ZMOD p] := by
            -- Use the multiplicative property of congruences.
            have h5 : (x ^ 2 : ℤ) ≡ a [ZMOD p] := h2
            have h6 : (y ^ 2 : ℤ) ≡ b [ZMOD p] := h3
            calc
              (x ^ 2 : ℤ) * y ^ 2 ≡ a * b [ZMOD p] := by
                gcongr
              _ = a * b := by rfl
          simpa [Int.ModEq] using h4
        _ = a * b := by rfl
    exact h1
  exact h_main

      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_image]

              have h₉ : m = 0 := by

        obtain ⟨m, hm₁, hm₂⟩ := h₇
        have h₈ : m ≤ M / k := by
          have h₉ : k * m ≤ M := by

            apply Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le (by positivity) |>.mpr
            <;> nlinarith

        refine' ⟨m, ⟨h₉, h₈⟩, _⟩
        <;> simp_all [hm₁]
        <;> ring_nf at *
        <;> omega
      · -- Prove the reverse direction: if n is in the image, then n is in the filtered set

        obtain ⟨m, ⟨h₂, h₃⟩, rfl⟩ := hn

theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_332604_0_gs0 (m : ℕ) (hm : m > 0) :

theorem xgv2_mathd_numbertheory_167_3 (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) (h2n : Nat.Prime n)  (a : ℕ) (h3 : a^n = 2) : a ^ (n + 1) % (a ^ 2) ≤ 2 ↔ a = 2 := by
  have hn' : n ≥ 2 := by
    omega

  have h_main : False := by
    have h₁ : a ≤ 1 := by
      by_contra h
      -- Assume a > 1, then a ≥ 2
      have h₂ : a ≥ 2 := by omega
      have h₃ : a ^ n ≥ 2 ^ n := by
        exact Nat.pow_le_pow_of_le_left h₂ n
      have h₄ : 2 ^ n ≥ 2 ^ 2 := by
        have h₅ : n ≥ 2 := hn'
        have h₆ : 2 ^ n ≥ 2 ^ 2 := by
          exact Nat.pow_le_pow_of_le_right (by norm_num) h₅
        exact h₆
      have h₅ : a ^ n ≥ 2 ^ n := h₃
      have h₆ : a ^ n ≥ 4 := by
        omega
      have h₇ : a ^ n = 2 := h3
      omega
    -- Now we know a ≤ 1, we can check the possible values of a
    have h₂ : a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by
      have h₃ : a ≤ 1 := h₁
      have h₄ : a ≥ 0 := by omega
      omega
    cases h₂ with
    | inl h₂ =>
      -- Case a = 0
      have h₃ : a = 0 := h₂
      rw [h₃] at h3
      have h₄ : (0 : ℕ) ^ n = 0 := by
        have h₅ : n ≠ 0 := by omega

      have h₆ : False := by
        omega
      exact h₆
    | inr h₂ =>
      -- Case a = 1
      have h₃ : a = 1 := h₂

      norm_num at h3
      <;> simp_all (config := {decide := true})

  have h_goal : a ^ (n + 1) % (a ^ 2) ≤ 2 ↔ a = 2 := by

theorem xstp_theorem_2019_p908 (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) (hn' : Nat.Prime n)  (x : ℕ → ℚ) (hx : ∀ i, x i = 1 / (2 * i)) : (∏ i in Finset.Icc 1 n, x i) ≤ (n + 1) / 2^n := by
  have h₀ : ∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, x i = 1 / (2 * i) := by
    intro i _
    exact hx i
  rw [Finset.prod_congr rfl h₀]
  have h₁ : ∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, 1 / (2 * i : ℚ) ≤ 1 / 2 := by
    intro i hi
    have : (0 : ℚ) < 2 * i := by
      norm_cast
      linarith [Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi]
    rw [div_le_div_iff] <;> norm_num <;> norm_cast
    <;> linarith [Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi]
  calc
    (∏ k in Finset.Icc 1 n, (1 / (2 * k : ℚ))) ≤ ∏ k in Finset.Icc 1 n, (1 / 2 : ℚ) := Finset.prod_le_prod (fun i _ ↦ by positivity) (fun i hi ↦ h₁ i hi)
    _ = (1 / 2) ^ n := by simp [Finset.prod_const]
    _ = 1 / (2 ^ n) := by field_simp
    _ ≤ (n + 1) / (2 ^ n) := by
      exact div_le_div_of_le_of_nonneg (by
        norm_cast
        linarith) (by positivity)
  <;> rfl
  <;> rfl
  <;> rfl

theorem xgv2_mathd_numbertheory_4177 (n : ℕ) (hn : Nat.Prime n)  ( hn' : n ≠ 2) :  (∑ k in Nat.properDivisors n, (1 : ℕ) / k) ≠ n^3 / n := by
  have h_n_ge_3 : n ≥ 3 := by
    have h₁ := hn.two_le
    have h₂ : n ≠ 2 := hn'
    have h₃ : n ≥ 3 := by
      by_contra h
      -- We know n ≥ 2 and n ≠ 2, so we check if n could be 2.
      interval_cases n <;> norm_num at h₁ h₂ ⊢ <;> try contradiction
      <;> try norm_num [Nat.Prime] at hn
    exact h₃
    <;> aesop

  have h_proper_divisors : Nat.properDivisors n = {1} := by
    have h₁ : n.Prime := hn
    have h₂ : n ≠ 2 := hn'
    have h₃ : n ≥ 3 := h_n_ge_3
    -- We need to show that the proper divisors of n are exactly {1}
    -- Since n is prime, its proper divisors are only 1.
    have h₄ : Nat.properDivisors n = {1} := by
      -- Use the fact that n is prime to conclude that the proper divisors are {1}
      have h₅ : ∀ d : ℕ, d ∣ n → d < n → d = 1 := by
        intro d hd hdn
        have h₆ : d = 1 ∨ d = n := by
          apply hn.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd d hd
        cases h₆ with
        | inl h₆ =>
          exact h₆
        | inr h₆ =>
          -- If d = n, then d < n is false, so this case is impossible
          have h₇ : d < n := hdn
          omega
      -- Use the fact that the proper divisors of n are exactly the divisors of n that are less than n
      have h₆ : Nat.properDivisors n = Finset.filter (fun d => d ∣ n) (Finset.Ico 1 n) := by
        rfl
      rw [h₆]
      -- Show that the only proper divisor of n is 1
      have h₇ : Finset.filter (fun d => d ∣ n) (Finset.Ico 1 n) = {1} := by
        apply Finset.ext
        intro d
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Ico, Finset.mem_singleton]
        constructor
        · intro h
          have h₈ : d ∣ n := h.2
          have h₉ : 1 ≤ d := h.1.1
          have h₁₀ : d < n := h.1.2
          have h₁₁ : d = 1 := h₅ d h₈ h₁₀
          simp_all
        · intro h
          have h₈ : d = 1 := h
          rw [h₈]
          simp [Nat.Prime.ne_zero hn, Nat.Prime.ne_one hn]
          <;> norm_num
          <;>
            (try omega)
          <;>
            (try
              {
                have h₉ := hn.two_le
                omega
              })
      rw [h₇]
    exact h₄

  have h_sum : (∑ k in Nat.properDivisors n, (1 : ℕ) / k) = 1 := by
    rw [h_proper_divisors]
    <;> simp [Finset.sum_singleton, Nat.div_self (Nat.Prime.pos hn)]
    <;> norm_num

  have h_n3_div_n : n ^ 3 / n = n ^ 2 := by
    have h₁ : n ≠ 0 := Nat.Prime.ne_zero hn
    have h₂ : n ^ 3 = n * n ^ 2 := by
      ring
    rw [h₂]
    have h₃ : n * n ^ 2 / n = n ^ 2 := by
      apply Nat.div_eq_of_eq_mul_left (Nat.Prime.pos hn)
      <;> ring
      <;> simp [Nat.mul_div_cancel_left _ (Nat.Prime.pos hn)]
    rw [h₃]

  have h_final : (∑ k in Nat.properDivisors n, (1 : ℕ) / k) ≠ n ^ 3 / n := by
    rw [h_sum, h_n3_div_n]
    have h₁ : n ≥ 3 := h_n_ge_3
    have h₂ : n ^ 2 > 1 := by
      nlinarith
    omega

  exact h_final

statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0 ∧ n ≠ 1) (hn' : 2 < n) : ((Finset.filter (fun x => x < n ∧ x^2∣ n ) ( Finset.range (n + 1))).card ≤ n)

theorem xgv2_math_3597_2014_p6 (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0 ∧ n ≠ 1) (hn' : 2 < n) :
            ((Finset.filter (fun x => x < n ∧ x^2∣ n ) ( Finset.range (n + 1))).card ≤ n) := by
  have h_subset : Finset.filter (fun x => x < n ∧ x^2 ∣ n) (Finset.range (n + 1)) ⊆ Finset.range n := by

    -- We need to show that if x is in the filtered set, then x < n.
    have h₁ : x < n + 1 := by omega
    have h₂ : x < n := by
      -- Extract the condition x < n from the filter.
      tauto
    -- Since x < n, x is in the range n.
    omega

  have h_card : (Finset.filter (fun x => x < n ∧ x^2 ∣ n) (Finset.range (n + 1))).card ≤ n := by
    have h₁ : (Finset.filter (fun x => x < n ∧ x^2 ∣ n) (Finset.range (n + 1))).card ≤ (Finset.range n).card := by
      apply Finset.card_le_of_subset h_subset
    have h₂ : (Finset.range n).card = n := by
      simp
    have h₃ : (Finset.filter (fun x => x < n ∧ x^2 ∣ n) (Finset.range (n + 1))).card ≤ n := by
      linarith
    exact h₃

  exact h_card

      intro h_dvd
      -- Assume 2^(k+1) ∣ n, then 2^(k+1) ∣ m * 2^k
      have h₁ : 2 ^ (k + 1) ∣ m * 2 ^ k := by
        rw [hm] at h_dvd
        exact h_dvd
      -- Since 2^(k+1) ∣ m * 2^k, we can write m * 2^k = 2^(k+1) * t for some t
      have h₂ : ∃ t, m * 2 ^ k = 2 ^ (k + 1) * t := by
        obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := h₁
        exact ⟨t, by linarith⟩
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := h₂
      -- Simplify the equation to m = 2 * t
      have h₃ : m = 2 * t := by
        have h₄ : m * 2 ^ k = 2 ^ (k + 1) * t := ht
        have h₅ : m * 2 ^ k = 2 * 2 ^ k * t := by
          calc
            m * 2 ^ k = 2 ^ (k + 1) * t := h₄
            _ = (2 * 2 ^ k) * t := by
              rw [pow_succ]
              <;> ring
            _ = 2 * 2 ^ k * t := by ring
        have h₆ : m * 2 ^ k = 2 * 2 ^ k * t := h₅
        have h₇ : m = 2 * t := by
          apply Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_right (show 0 < 2 ^ k by
            apply Nat.pos_pow_of_pos
            norm_num)
          linarith
        exact h₇
      -- m is odd, so 2 ∣ m is false
      have h₄ : ¬(2 ∣ m) := by
        cases' hm_odd with t ht
        rw [ht]
        <;> simp [Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero, Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, Nat.mod_mod]
        <;> omega
      -- Contradiction arises as 2 ∣ m is false
      have h₅ : 2 ∣ m := by
        rw [h₃]
        <;> simp [Nat.dvd_mul_right]
      exact h₄ h₅
  exact h_main

statement: (n m : ℕ) (h₀ : 1 < n ∧ 1 < m) (h₁ : n.Prime ∧ m.Prime) (h₂ : n^n * m^m ∣ n * m) : n ≡ m [MOD n * m] ↔ n = m

theorem xstp_mathd_numbertheory_752 (n m : ℕ) (h₀ : 1 < n ∧ 1 < m) (h₁ : n.Prime ∧ m.Prime) (h₂ : n^n * m^m ∣ n * m) : n ≡ m [MOD n * m] ↔ n = m := by

statement: (n w h : ℕ) (total_sq : n = 40) (rect_dim : n = w * h) (multiple_rows : h > 1) (has_middle_row : h % 2 = 1) : n - w = 32

proofs.proof:
theorem xgpset_1196873 (n w h : ℕ)
  (total_sq : n = 40)
  (rect_dim : n = w * h)
  (multiple_rows : h > 1)
  (has_middle_row : h % 2 = 1) :
  n - w = 32 := by
  have h_divides_40 : h ∣ 40 := by
    have h₁ : w * h = 40 := by
      linarith
    have h₂ : h ∣ 40 := by
      use w
      linarith
    exact h₂

  have h_eq_5 : h = 5 := by
    have h₁ : h ∣ 40 := h_divides_40
    have h₂ : h > 1 := multiple_rows
    have h₃ : h % 2 = 1 := has_middle_row
    have h₄ : h ≤ 40 := by
      have h₅ : h ∣ 40 := h_divides_40
      exact Nat.le_of_dvd (by norm_num) h₅
    -- We now check all possible odd divisors of 40 greater than 1
    interval_cases h <;> norm_num at h₁ h₃ ⊢ <;>
      (try omega) <;>
      (try {
        have h₅ : w ≤ 40 := by
          nlinarith
        interval_cases w <;> norm_num at rect_dim ⊢ <;>
          (try omega) <;>
          (try nlinarith)
      })
    <;>
    omega

  have w_eq_8 : w = 8 := by
    have h₁ : w * h = 40 := by
      linarith
    rw [h_eq_5] at h₁
    have h₂ : w * 5 = 40 := by
      linarith
    have h₃ : w = 8 := by
      omega
    exact h₃

  have final_result : n - w = 32 := by
    rw [total_sq, w_eq_8]
    <;> norm_num
    <;> omega

  apply final_result

statement: (p : ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hN : N ≥ p) : p ∣ Nat.factorial N + N ↔ p ∣ N

proofs.proof:
theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_326506_1_gs3 (p : ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hN : N ≥ p) :
  p ∣ Nat.factorial N + N ↔ p ∣ N := by
  have h_imp : p ∣ Nat.factorial N + N → p ∣ N := by
    intro h
    by_contra h₁
    have h₂ : p ∣ Nat.factorial N := by
      -- Since p is a prime and p ≤ N, p divides N!
      have h₃ : p ≤ N := by linarith
      have h₄ : p ∣ Nat.factorial N := by
        apply Nat.dvd_factorial
        · exact Nat.Prime.pos hp
        · linarith
      exact h₄
    -- Since p divides both N! and N! + N, it divides (N! + N) - N! = N
    have h₅ : p ∣ Nat.factorial N + N := h
    have h₆ : p ∣ Nat.factorial N + N - Nat.factorial N := Nat.dvd_sub' h₅ h₂
    have h₇ : Nat.factorial N + N - Nat.factorial N = N := by
      have h₈ : Nat.factorial N ≤ Nat.factorial N + N := by
        apply Nat.le_add_right
      have h₉ : Nat.factorial N + N - Nat.factorial N = N := by
        omega
      exact h₉
    rw [h₇] at h₆
    exact h₁ h₆

  have h_conv : p ∣ N → p ∣ Nat.factorial N + N := by
    intro h
    have h₁ : p ∣ Nat.factorial N + N := by
      -- Use the fact that p divides N to show it divides N! + N
      have h₂ : p ∣ N := h
      have h₃ : p ∣ Nat.factorial N := by
        -- Since p is a prime and p ≤ N, p divides N!
        have h₄ : p ≤ N := by linarith
        have h₅ : p ∣ Nat.factorial N := by
          apply Nat.dvd_factorial
          · exact Nat.Prime.pos hp
          · linarith
        exact h₅
      -- Since p divides both N! and N, it divides their sum
      have h₆ : p ∣ Nat.factorial N + N := by
        exact Nat.dvd_add h₃ h₂
      exact h₆
    exact h₁

  have h_main : p ∣ Nat.factorial N + N ↔ p ∣ N := by
    constructor
    · -- Prove the forward direction: if p ∣ N! + N, then p ∣ N
      exact h_imp
    · -- Prove the backward direction: if p ∣ N, then p ∣ N! + N
      exact h_conv

  exact h_main

statement: (p : ℕ) (a : ℤ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (h : a^2 ≡ a - 3 [ZMOD p]) : 9 * a^2 - 9 * a + 27 ≡ 0 [ZMOD p]

theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_368435_0_gs1 (p : ℕ) (a : ℤ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (h : a^2 ≡ a - 3 [ZMOD p]) :
  9 * a^2 - 9 * a + 27 ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by
  have h_main : 9 * a^2 - 9 * a + 27 ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by
    have h₁ : a ^ 2 ≡ a - 3 [ZMOD p] := h
    have h₂ : (a ^ 2 : ℤ) - a + 3 ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by
      -- Use the given congruence to derive the desired congruence
      have h₃ : a ^ 2 ≡ a - 3 [ZMOD p] := h₁
      have h₄ : (a ^ 2 : ℤ) ≡ (a - 3 : ℤ) [ZMOD p] := by exact_mod_cast h₃
      -- Simplify the congruence to find the desired form
      have h₅ : (a ^ 2 : ℤ) - a + 3 ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by
        -- Use the given congruence to find the desired form
        have h₅₁ : (a ^ 2 : ℤ) - a + 3 = (a ^ 2 : ℤ) - (a - 3 : ℤ) := by
          ring
        rw [h₅₁]
        simp_all [Int.ModEq, Int.emod_eq_emod_iff_emod_sub_eq_zero]
        <;>
        (try omega) <;>
        (try simp_all [Int.emod_eq_emod_iff_emod_sub_eq_zero]) <;>
        (try omega) <;>
        (try linarith) <;>
        (try ring_nf at *) <;>
        (try omega)
        <;>
        omega
      exact h₅
    -- Use the derived congruence to find the final result
    have h₃ : (9 * a ^ 2 - 9 * a + 27 : ℤ) ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by
      have h₄ : (9 * a ^ 2 - 9 * a + 27 : ℤ) = 9 * ((a ^ 2 - a + 3 : ℤ)) := by
        ring
      rw [h₄]
      have h₅ : (9 : ℤ) * ((a ^ 2 - a + 3 : ℤ)) ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by
        have h₆ : (a ^ 2 - a + 3 : ℤ) ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := h₂
        have h₇ : (9 : ℤ) * ((a ^ 2 - a + 3 : ℤ)) ≡ (9 : ℤ) * (0 : ℤ) [ZMOD p] := by
          exact Int.ModEq.mul_left (9 : ℤ) h₆
        simpa [Int.ModEq, Int.emod_eq_emod_iff_emod_sub_eq_zero] using h₇
      exact h₅
    exact h₃
  exact h_main

statement: (p : ℕ) (a : ℤ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (ha_not_div : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a) (ha_cube : a^3 ≡ 1 [ZMOD p]) (ha_order : orderOf (a : ZMod p) = 3) : a^2 + a + 1 ≡ 0 [ZMOD p]

theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_38414_0_gs0_f0_gs2 (p : ℕ) (a : ℤ) (hp : Nat.Prime p)
    (ha_not_div : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a) (ha_cube : a^3 ≡ 1 [ZMOD p])
    (ha_order : orderOf (a : ZMod p) = 3) :
    a^2 + a + 1 ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by
  have h_main : a^2 + a + 1 ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by
    haveI := Fact.mk hp
    have h₁ : (a : ZMod p) ^ 3 = 1 := by
      rw [← ZMod.int_cast_eq_int_cast_iff] at ha_cube
      simpa [pow_three] using ha_cube
    have h₂ : orderOf (a : ZMod p) = 3 := ha_order
    have h₃ : (a : ZMod p) ^ 2 ≠ 1 := by
      intro h
      have h₄ : orderOf (a : ZMod p) ∣ 2 := by
        apply orderOf_dvd_of_pow_eq_one
        simpa [h, pow_two, pow_three] using h₁
      rw [h₂] at h₄
      norm_num at h₄
      <;> contradiction
    have h₄ : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 1 := by
      intro h
      have h₅ : orderOf (a : ZMod p) ∣ 1 := by
        apply orderOf_dvd_of_pow_eq_one
        simpa [h, pow_one] using h₁
      rw [h₂] at h₅
      norm_num at h₅
      <;> contradiction
    have h₅ : (a : ZMod p) - 1 ≠ 0 := by
      intro h₅
      have h₆ : (a : ZMod p) = 1 := by
        simpa [sub_eq_zero] using h₅
      contradiction
    have h₆ : (a : ZMod p) ^ 3 - 1 = 0 := by
      simpa [sub_eq_zero] using h₁
    have h₇ : ((a : ZMod p) ^ 3 - 1 : ZMod p) = 0 := by simpa using h₆
    have h₈ : ((a : ZMod p) - 1 : ZMod p) * ((a : ZMod p) ^ 2 + (a : ZMod p) + 1) = 0 := by
      have h₉ : ((a : ZMod p) ^ 3 - 1 : ZMod p) = ((a : ZMod p) - 1 : ZMod p) * ((a : ZMod p) ^ 2 + (a : ZMod p) + 1) := by
        ring_nf
        <;> simp [pow_two, pow_three]
        <;> ring_nf
        <;> norm_num
        <;> omega
      simpa [h₉] using h₇
    have h₉ : ((a : ZMod p) - 1 : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := by
      exact h₅
    have h₁₀ : ((a : ZMod p) ^ 2 + (a : ZMod p) + 1 : ZMod p) = 0 := by
      apply mul_left_cancel₀ h₉
      simpa using h₈
    have h₁₁ : a ^ 2 + a + 1 ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by
      rw [← ZMod.int_cast_eq_int_cast_iff]
      simp_all [Int.ModEq, Int.emod_eq_emod_iff_emod_sub_eq_zero]
      <;> ring_nf at * <;> simp_all [sub_eq_add_neg]
      <;> omega
    exact h₁₁
  exact h_main

statement: (p : ℕ) (a : ℤ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hmod : p % 4 = 3) : ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ (a^2 + 1)

proofs.proof:
theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_372757_0_gs4_f0_gs2 (p : ℕ) (a : ℤ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hmod : p % 4 = 3) :
  ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ (a^2 + 1) := by
  have h₁ : (p : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := by
    have h₂ : p % 4 = 3 := hmod
    have h₃ : p % 2 = 1 := by omega
    exact_mod_cast h₃

  have h₂ : p ≥ 3 := by
    have h₃ := Nat.Prime.two_le hp
    have h₄ : p % 4 = 3 := hmod
    have h₅ : p ≠ 2 := by
      by_contra h
      rw [h] at h₄
      norm_num at h₄ ⊢
    have h₆ : p ≥ 3 := by
      by_contra h₇
      interval_cases p <;> norm_num at h₄ h₅ hp ⊢ <;> contradiction
    exact h₆

  have h₃ : ∀ (a : ℤ), (p : ℤ) ∣ (a^2 + 1) → False := by
    intro a h
    have h₄ : (p : ℤ) ∣ (a^2 + 1) := h
    have h₅ : (p : ℤ) ∣ a → False := by
      intro h₅
      have h₆ : (p : ℤ) ∣ (a^2 + 1) := h₄
      have h₇ : (p : ℤ) ∣ a^2 := by
        have h₈ : (p : ℤ) ∣ a := h₅
        have h₉ : (p : ℤ) ∣ a^2 := by
          exact dvd_pow h₈ (by norm_num)
        exact h₉
      have h₈ : (p : ℤ) ∣ 1 := by
        have h₉ : (p : ℤ) ∣ (a^2 + 1 - a^2) := by
          exact dvd_sub h₆ h₇
        simpa using h₉
      have h₉ : (p : ℕ) ∣ 1 := by
        norm_cast at h₈ ⊢
        <;> simpa using h₈
      have h₁₀ : p ∣ 1 := by simpa using h₉
      have h₁₁ : p ≥ 3 := h₂
      have h₁₂ : p ≤ 1 := by
        exact Nat.le_of_dvd (by norm_num) h₁₀
      linarith
    have h₆ : ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ a := by
      intro h₇
      exact h₅ h₇
    -- We need to show that if p does not divide a, then we get a contradiction.
    have h₇ : (p : ℕ) % 4 = 3 := by exact_mod_cast hmod
    have h₈ : (p : ℕ) ≥ 3 := h₂
    -- Use the fact that p ≡ 3 mod 4 to derive a contradiction.
    have h₉ : (p : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := h₁
    have h₁₀ : (p : ℕ) % 4 = 3 := by exact_mod_cast hmod
    -- Use Fermat's Little Theorem and properties of quadratic residues to derive a contradiction.
    have h₁₁ : (p : ℤ) ∣ (a^2 + 1) := h₄
    have h₁₂ : ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ a := h₆
    -- Use the fact that a and p are coprime to derive a contradiction.
    have h₁₃ : (a : ℤ) ^ 2 + 1 ≡ 0 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
      rw [Int.ModEq]
      exact Int.emod_eq_zero_of_dvd h₁₁
    have h₁₄ : (a : ℤ) ^ 2 ≡ -1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
      have h₁₅ : (a : ℤ) ^ 2 + 1 ≡ 0 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := h₁₃
      have h₁₆ : (a : ℤ) ^ 2 ≡ -1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
        calc
          (a : ℤ) ^ 2 ≡ (a : ℤ) ^ 2 + 1 - 1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
            simp [Int.ModEq, Int.emod_emod]
          _ ≡ 0 - 1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
            simpa [Int.ModEq, Int.emod_emod] using Int.ModEq.sub h₁₅ (Int.ModEq.refl 1)
          _ = -1 := by ring
          _ ≡ -1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by rfl
      exact h₁₆
    have h₁₅ : (a : ℤ) ^ (p - 1 : ℕ) ≡ 1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
      haveI := Fact.mk hp
      have h₁₆ : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0 := by
        intro h₁₇
        have h₁₈ : (p : ℤ) ∣ a := by
          have h₁₉ : (a : ZMod p) = 0 := h₁₇
          have h₂₀ : (p : ℤ) ∣ a := by
            simpa [ZMod.int_cast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd] using h₁₉
          exact h₂₀
        exact h₆ h₁₈
      have h₁₇ : (a : ZMod p) ^ (p - 1) = 1 := by
        apply ZMod.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one
        exact h₁₆
      have h₁₈ : (a : ℤ) ^ (p - 1 : ℕ) ≡ 1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
        have h₁₉ : (a : ZMod p) ^ (p - 1) = 1 := h₁₇
        have h₂₀ : (a : ℤ) ^ (p - 1 : ℕ) ≡ 1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
          rw [← ZMod.int_cast_eq_int_cast_iff]
          simpa [ZMod.int_cast_eq_int_cast_iff] using h₁₉
        exact h₂₀
      exact h₁₈
    have h₁₆ : (a : ℤ) ^ (p - 1 : ℕ) ≡ -1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
      have h₁₇ : (a : ℤ) ^ 2 ≡ -1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := h₁₄
      have h₁₈ : (a : ℤ) ^ (2 * ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2)) ≡ (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
        have h₁₉ : (a : ℤ) ^ (2 * ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2)) = ((a : ℤ) ^ 2) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) := by
          ring_nf
          <;> simp [pow_mul]
        rw [h₁₉]
        have h₂₀ : ((a : ℤ) ^ 2 : ℤ) ≡ (-1 : ℤ) [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := h₁₇
        have h₂₁ : (((a : ℤ) ^ 2 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) : ℤ) ≡ (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
          calc
            (((a : ℤ) ^ 2 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) : ℤ) ≡ ((-1 : ℤ) : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
              simpa [Int.ModEq] using Int.ModEq.pow ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) h₂₀
            _ = (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) := by rfl
        exact h₂₁
      have h₁₉ : (2 : ℕ) * ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) = p - 1 := by
        have h₂₀ : (p : ℕ) % 4 = 3 := hmod
        have h₂₁ : p % 2 = 1 := h₁
        have h₂₂ : (p : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := h₁
        have h₂₃ : (p : ℕ) % 4 = 3 := hmod
        have h₂₄ : (p - 1 : ℕ) % 2 = 0 := by
          omega
        have h₂₅ : (p - 1 : ℕ) / 2 * 2 = p - 1 := by
          have h₂₆ : (p - 1 : ℕ) % 2 = 0 := h₂₄
          have h₂₇ : (p - 1 : ℕ) / 2 * 2 = p - 1 := by
            have h₂₈ : (p - 1 : ℕ) % 2 = 0 := h₂₆
            have h₂₉ : (p - 1 : ℕ) / 2 * 2 = p - 1 := by
              omega
            exact h₂₉
          exact h₂₇
        omega
      have h₂₀ : (a : ℤ) ^ (p - 1 : ℕ) ≡ (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
        have h₂₁ : (a : ℤ) ^ (2 * ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2)) ≡ (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := h₁₈
        have h₂₂ : (a : ℤ) ^ (2 * ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2)) = (a : ℤ) ^ (p - 1 : ℕ) := by
          rw [h₁₉]
          <;> ring_nf
          <;> simp [pow_add, pow_mul]
        rw [h₂₂] at h₂₁
        exact h₂₁
      have h₂₁ : ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2 : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := by
        have h₂₂ : (p : ℕ) % 4 = 3 := hmod
        have h₂₃ : (p : ℕ) ≥ 3 := h₂
        have h₂₄ : (p : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := h₁
        have h₂₅ : ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2 : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := by
          have h₂₆ : (p : ℕ) % 4 = 3 := hmod
          have h₂₇ : (p : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := h₁
          have h₂₈ : ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2 : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := by
            omega
          exact h₂₈
        exact h₂₅
      have h₂₂ : (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) = -1 := by
        have h₂₃ : ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2 : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := h₂₁
        have h₂₄ : (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) = -1 := by
          have h₂₅ : ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2 : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := h₂₁
          have h₂₆ : (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) = -1 := by
            rw [← Nat.mod_add_div (((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) : ℕ) 2]
            simp [h₂₅, pow_add, pow_mul, pow_one, Int.mul_emod, Int.add_emod, Int.emod_emod]
            <;> norm_num <;> ring_nf at * <;> omega
          exact h₂₆
        exact h₂₄
      have h₂₃ : (a : ℤ) ^ (p - 1 : ℕ) ≡ -1 [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := by
        have h₂₄ : (a : ℤ) ^ (p - 1 : ℕ) ≡ (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) [ZMOD (p : ℤ)] := h₂₀
        have h₂₅ : (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1 : ℕ) / 2) = -1 := h₂₂
        rw [h₂₅] at h₂₄

    <;>

    <;>

    <;>

      have h₃ : (p : ℤ) * ((p : ℤ) ^ 2 - 3 * (p : ℤ) * a + 3 * a ^ 2) ≡ 0 [ZMOD p] := by

      exact h₃

      ring_nf
      <;> omega
    rw [h₂]
    -- Use the result from h₁ to conclude the proof
    have h₃ : 1 + ((p : ℤ) ^ 3 - 3 * (p : ℤ) ^ 2 * a + 3 * (p : ℤ) * a ^ 2) ≡ 1 [ZMOD p] := by
      -- Use the fact that the expression is congruent to 0 modulo p

        exact Int.ModEq.add (Int.ModEq.refl 1) h₄
      -- Simplify the right-hand side
      have h₆ : 1 + (0 : ℤ) = (1 : ℤ) := by ring

    exact h₃

statement: (p : ℕ) (h₀ : Nat.Prime p) : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) ≤ p^2

theorem xgv2_lean_workbook_51263 (p : ℕ) (h₀ : Nat.Prime p) : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) ≤ p^2 := by
  have h₁ : p ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le h₀
  have h₂ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) ≤ 1 := by
    have h₃ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) ≤ 1 := by
      by_cases h₄ : p = 2
      · -- Case p = 2
        rw [h₄]
        norm_num [Finset.sum_Ico_succ_top, Nat.div_eq_of_lt]
        <;> rfl
      · -- Case p ≥ 3
        have h₅ : p ≥ 3 := by
          by_contra h₅
          have h₆ : p < 3 := by linarith
          have h₇ : p = 2 := by
            omega
          contradiction
        have h₆ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) = 1 := by
          have h₇ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) = ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) := rfl
          rw [h₇]
          -- We need to show that the sum is 1
          -- The only non-zero term is when k = p - 1
          have h₈ : p - 1 ∈ Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2) := by
            -- Prove that p - 1 is in the interval [2, p + 1]
            have h₉ : 2 ≤ p - 1 := by
              omega
            have h₁₀ : p - 1 < p + 2 := by
              omega
            exact Finset.mem_Ico.mpr ⟨h₉, h₁₀⟩
          have h₉ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) = 1 := by
            -- Calculate the sum
            have h₁₀ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) = ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) := by
              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
              intro k hk
              have h₁₁ : k ∈ Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2) := hk
              have h₁₂ : 2 ≤ k ∧ k < p + 2 := Finset.mem_Ico.mp h₁₁
              have h₁₃ : 2 ≤ k := h₁₂.1
              have h₁₄ : k < p + 2 := h₁₂.2
              by_cases h₁₅ : k = p - 1
              · -- Case k = p - 1
                have h₁₆ : k = p - 1 := h₁₅
                have h₁₇ : p - k = 1 := by
                  rw [h₁₆]
                  have h₁₈ : p ≥ 3 := h₅
                  have h₁₉ : p - (p - 1) = 1 := by
                    have h₂₀ : p - 1 ≤ p := by omega
                    have h₂₁ : p - (p - 1) = 1 := by
                      omega
                    exact h₂₁
                  exact h₁₉
                have h₂₂ : 1 / (p - k) = 1 := by
                  rw [h₁₇]
                  <;> norm_num
                rw [h₂₂]
                simp [h₁₅]
              · -- Case k ≠ p - 1
                have h₁₆ : k ≠ p - 1 := h₁₅
                have h₁₇ : 1 / (p - k) = 0 := by
                  by_cases h₁₈ : p - k = 0
                  · -- Case p - k = 0
                    rw [h₁₈]
                    <;> norm_num
                  · -- Case p - k ≠ 0
                    have h₁₉ : p - k ≥ 2 := by
                      by_contra h₁₉
                      have h₂₀ : p - k < 2 := by omega
                      have h₂₁ : p - k = 1 := by
                        omega
                      have h₂₂ : k = p - 1 := by
                        have h₂₃ : p - k = 1 := h₂₁
                        have h₂₄ : k ≤ p := by omega
                        have h₂₅ : p - k = 1 := h₂₁
                        have h₂₆ : k = p - 1 := by
                          omega
                        exact h₂₆
                      contradiction
                    have h₂₃ : 1 / (p - k) = 0 := by
                      have h₂₄ : p - k ≥ 2 := h₁₉
                      have h₂₅ : 1 / (p - k) = 0 := by
                        apply Nat.div_eq_of_lt
                        <;> omega
                      exact h₂₅
                    exact h₂₃
                rw [h₁₇]
                simp [h₁₆]
            rw [h₁₀]
            -- Calculate the sum of the indicator function
            have h₂₀ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) = 1 := by
              have h₂₁ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) = ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) := rfl
              rw [h₂₁]
              -- Use the fact that p - 1 is in the interval and all other terms are 0
              have h₂₂ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) = 1 := by
                have h₂₃ : p - 1 ∈ Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2) := h₈
                have h₂₄ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) = 1 := by
                  -- Use the fact that p - 1 is the only term that contributes 1
                  have h₂₅ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) = ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) := rfl
                  rw [h₂₅]
                  -- Use the fact that p - 1 is the only term that contributes 1
                  have h₂₆ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) = 1 := by
                    -- Use the fact that p - 1 is the only term that contributes 1
                    calc
                      _ = ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) := rfl
                      _ = 1 := by
                        -- Use the fact that p - 1 is the only term that contributes 1
                        have h₂₇ : p - 1 ∈ Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2) := h₈
                        have h₂₈ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) = 1 := by
                          -- Use the fact that p - 1 is the only term that contributes 1
                          calc
                            _ = ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) := rfl
                            _ = 1 := by
                              -- Use the fact that p - 1 is the only term that contributes 1
                              have h₂₉ : p - 1 ∈ Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2) := h₈
                              have h₃₀ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (if k = p - 1 then 1 else 0) = 1 := by
                                -- Use the fact that p - 1 is the only term that contributes 1
                                simp_all [Finset.sum_ite, Finset.filter_eq', Finset.filter_ne']
                                <;>
                                (try omega) <;>
                                (try aesop) <;>
                                (try
                                  {
                                    have h₃₁ : p - 1 < p + 2 := by omega
                                    have h₃₂ : 2 ≤ p - 1 := by omega
                                    interval_cases p <;> simp_all (config := {decide := true})
                                  })
                              exact h₃₀
                        exact h₂₈
                  exact h₂₆
                exact h₂₄
              exact h₂₂
            exact h₂₀
          exact h₉
        rw [h₆]
        <;> norm_num
    exact h₃
  have h₃ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) ≤ p^2 := by
    have h₄ : p ≥ 2 := h₁
    have h₅ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) ≤ 1 := h₂
    have h₆ : 1 ≤ p ^ 2 := by
      have h₇ : p ≥ 2 := h₁
      have h₈ : 1 ≤ p ^ 2 := by
        nlinarith
      exact h₈
    have h₇ : ∑ k in Finset.Ico 2 (p + 2), (1 / (p - k)) ≤ p ^ 2 := by
      calc
        _ ≤ 1 := h₅
        _ ≤ p ^ 2 := by
          have h₈ : p ≥ 2 := h₁
          have h₉ : 1 ≤ p ^ 2 := by nlinarith
          linarith
    exact h₇
  exact h₃

statement: (p : ℕ) (h₁ : Nat.Prime p) (h₂ : p ≠ 2) : p ≠ 6 * (p + 1) % (p + 1)^2

proofs.proof:
theorem xgv2_lean_201378052 (p : ℕ) (h₁ : Nat.Prime p) (h₂ : p ≠ 2)  : p ≠ 6 * (p + 1) % (p + 1)^2 := by
  have h_main : p ≠ 6 * (p + 1) % (p + 1)^2 := by
    intro h
    have h₃ := h₁.two_le
    have h₄ : p ≥ 3 := by
      by_contra h₅
      have h₆ : p ≤ 2 := by omega
      interval_cases p <;> norm_num at h₁ h₂ h ⊢ <;> contradiction
    have h₅ : p ≠ 2 := h₂
    have h₆ : p % 2 = 1 := by
      have h₇ := h₁.eq_two_or_odd
      omega
    -- We will consider the cases p = 3, p = 5, and p ≥ 7 separately
    have h₇ : p = 3 ∨ p = 5 ∨ p ≥ 7 := by
      have h₈ := h₁.two_le
      have h₉ : p ≥ 3 := by omega
      have h₁₀ : p % 2 = 1 := by omega
      have h₁₁ : p ≠ 2 := h₂
      have h₁₂ : p = 3 ∨ p = 5 ∨ p ≥ 7 := by
        by_cases h₁₃ : p ≥ 7
        · exact Or.inr (Or.inr h₁₃)
        · have h₁₄ : p ≤ 6 := by omega
          interval_cases p <;> norm_num at h₁ h₆ h₅ ⊢ <;> try contradiction <;> try omega
      exact h₁₂
    rcases h₇ with (rfl | rfl | h₇)
    · -- Case p = 3
      norm_num at h ⊢ <;>
      omega
    · -- Case p = 5
      norm_num at h ⊢ <;>
      omega
    · -- Case p ≥ 7
      have h₈ : 6 * (p + 1) % (p + 1) ^ 2 = 6 * (p + 1) := by
        have h₉ : 6 * (p + 1) < (p + 1) ^ 2 := by
          cases p with
          | zero => contradiction
          | succ p' =>
            cases p' with
            | zero => contradiction
            | succ p'' =>
              cases p'' with
              | zero => contradiction
              | succ p''' =>
                simp [Nat.mul_succ, Nat.pow_succ, Nat.add_assoc]
                ring_nf
                <;>
                (try omega) <;>
                (try nlinarith) <;>
                (try ring_nf at * <;> omega) <;>
                (try omega)
        have h₁₀ : 6 * (p + 1) % (p + 1) ^ 2 = 6 * (p + 1) := by
          rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h₉]
        exact h₁₀
      rw [h₈] at h
      norm_num at h ⊢
      <;>
      (try omega) <;>
      (try nlinarith)
      <;>
      (try
        {
          have h₉ := h₁.two_le
          have h₁₀ := h₁.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 2
          have h₁₁ := h₁.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 3
          have h₁₂ := h₁.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 5
          have h₁₃ := h₁.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 7
          omega
        })
      <;>
      (try
        {
          omega
        })
  exact h_main

statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (a : ℕ) (h₀ : a ^ p ∣ p) : a ≡ 0 [MOD p] ↔ a = p

theorem xstp_theorem208 (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]  (a : ℕ) (h₀ : a ^ p ∣ p) : a ≡ 0  [MOD p] ↔ a = p := by
  have h₁ := (Fact.out : Nat.Prime p)
  have h₂ : a ^ p ∣ p := h₀
  have h₃ : a ∣ p := by
    have h₄ : a ^ p ∣ p := h₂
    exact Nat.dvd_of_pow_dvd (by linarith [h₁.two_le]) h₄
  have h₄ : a ≤ p := Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.Prime.pos h₁) h₃
  have h₅ : a ≡ 0 [MOD p] ↔ a = p := by
    constructor
    · intro h
      rw [Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd] at h
      have h₆ : a ^ p ∣ p := h₂
      have h₇ : a ∣ p := h₃
      exact (Nat.dvd_prime h₁).mp h₇ |>.resolve_left (by aesop)
    · intro h
      rw [h]
      simp [Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd, Nat.dvd_refl]
  exact h₅

statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (a : ℕ) (h₁ : a^p = 2) : a ^ (p*2) % p = 2 ↔ p = 2

theorem xstp_theorem19826 (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (a : ℕ) (h₁ : a^p = 2) : a ^ (p*2) % p = 2 ↔ p = 2 := by
  have h₃ : a ^ p = 2 := h₁
  have h₄ : p ≠ 0 := Fact.out (p := p.Prime).ne_zero
  have h₅ : p ≠ 1 := Fact.out (p := p.Prime).ne_one
  have h₆ : a = 1 := by
    by_contra h
    have : a ^ p > 2 := by
      have : a ≥ 2 := by
        by_contra h₇
        interval_cases a <;> simp_all
      have : a ^ p ≥ 2 ^ p := by
        exact pow_le_pow_of_le_left (by linarith) (by linarith) p
      have : 2 ^ p ≥ 4 := by
        have : p ≥ 2 := by
          by_contra h₇
          interval_cases p <;> simp_all
        have : 2 ^ p ≥ 2 ^ 2 := by
          exact pow_le_pow_of_le_right (by linarith) (by linarith)
        linarith
      linarith
    linarith
  simp_all

statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hp : 2 < p) (G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G] [Fact (Fintype.card G = p)] (x : G) : x * x ≠ 1 ↔ orderOf x > 2

proofs.proof:
theorem xstp_theorem_exercise_26248_24 (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
        (hp : 2 < p)
        (G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G] [Fact (Fintype.card G = p)] (x : G) :
        x * x ≠ 1 ↔ orderOf x > 2 := by
  have h1 : orderOf x ∣ p := by
        rw [← Fact.out (p := Fintype.card G = p)]
        exact orderOf_dvd_card
  have h2 : Nat.Prime p := Fact.out (p := p.Prime)
  have h3 : orderOf x ∣ p := by
        rw [← Fact.out (p := Fintype.card G = p)]
        exact orderOf_dvd_card
  have h4 : orderOf x = 1 ∨ orderOf x = p := by
        rw [Nat.dvd_prime h2] at h3
        tauto
  have h5 : x * x = 1 ↔ orderOf x ∣ 2:= by
        rw [← pow_two]
        rw [← orderOf_dvd_iff_pow_eq_one]
        <;> omega
  rcases h4 with (h4 | h4) <;> simp_all [Nat.dvd_prime Nat.prime_two]
  <;> omega

theorem xstp_theorem_exercise_26248_24 (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
        (hp : 2 < p)
        (G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G] [Fact (Fintype.card G = p)] (x : G) :
        x * x ≠ 1 ↔ orderOf x > 2 := by
  have h₁ : orderOf x ∣ p := by
    rw [← Fact.out (p := Fintype.card G = p)]
    exact orderOf_dvd_card
  have h₂ : Nat.Prime p := Fact.out (p := p.Prime)
  have h₃ : orderOf x = 1 ∨ orderOf x = p := by
    have h₄ : orderOf x ∣ p := h₁
    exact h₂.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd _ h₄
  constructor
  intro h
  have h₄ : orderOf x > 2 := by
    cases' h₃ with h₃ h₃ <;> simp_all [orderOf_eq_one_iff, h₂.one_lt]
      <;> omega
  exact h₄
  intro h
  have h₄ : x * x ≠ 1 := by
    intro h₅
    have h₆ : orderOf x ∣ 2 := by
      rw [orderOf_dvd_iff_pow_eq_one]
      simp_all [pow_two, mul_one]
    have h₇ : orderOf x = 1 ∨ orderOf x = 2 := by
      have h₈ : orderOf x ∣ 2 := h₆
      exact Nat.Prime.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd Nat.prime_two _ h₈
    cases' h₇ with h₇ h₇ <;> simp_all [orderOf_eq_one_iff, Nat.Prime.ne_one Nat.prime_two]
      <;> omega
  exact h₄

theorem xstp_exercise_23_4 (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hp : p ≠ 2) {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]

theorem xgv2_theorem_exercise_1970_241 (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (h₀ : p ≠ 4 ∧ p ≠ 3) ( a : ℕ) (h₁ : a^p = p ∧  p ∣ a) : a ^ (p - 1) * p ≠ 5 * (a / p) := by

    have h₂₁ : Nat.Prime p := Fact.out (p := Nat.Prime p)
    exact Nat.Prime.two_le h₂₁

  have h₃ : a = 0 ∨ a ≥ 1 := by
    by_cases h : a = 0
    · exact Or.inl h
    · exact Or.inr (by
        have h₄ : a ≥ 1 := by
          omega
        exact h₄)

  have h₄ : False := by
    have h₄₁ : a^p = p := h₁.1
    have h₄₂ : p ∣ a := h₁.2
    have h₄₃ : a = 0 ∨ a ≥ 1 := h₃
    cases h₄₃ with
    | inl h₄₄ =>
      -- Case: a = 0

      have h₄₆ : (0 : ℕ) ^ p = p := by simpa using h₄₁
      have h₄₇ : p = 0 := by
        by_cases h₄₈ : p = 0
        · exact h₄₈
        · have h₄₉ : p ≥ 2 := h₂
          have h₄₁₀ : (0 : ℕ) ^ p = 0 := by
            have h₄₁₁ : p ≠ 0 := by omega
            simp [h₄₁₁, pow_eq_zero_iff]
          rw [h₄₁₀] at h₄₆
          omega
      have h₄₁₁ : Nat.Prime p := Fact.out (p := Nat.Prime p)
      have h₄₁₂ : p ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le h₄₁₁
      omega
    | inr h₄₄ =>
      -- Case: a ≥ 1
      have h₄₅ : a ≥ 1 := h₄₄
      have h₄₆ : p ∣ a := h₄₂
      have h₄₇ : a ≥ p := by
        have h₄₇₁ : p ∣ a := h₄₆
        have h₄₇₂ : p ≤ a := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) h₄₇₁
        omega
      have h₄₈ : a ^ p ≥ p ^ p := by
        calc
          a ^ p ≥ p ^ p := by
            exact Nat.pow_le_pow_of_le_left (by omega) p
          _ = p ^ p := by rfl

        have h₄₉₁ : p ≥ 2 := h₂
        have h₄₉₂ : p ^ p ≥ p ^ 2 := by

          calc
            p ^ p ≥ p ^ 2 := h₄₉₂
            _ > p := h₄₉₃
        exact h₄₉₄
      have h₄₁₀ : a ^ p > p := by
        calc
          a ^ p ≥ p ^ p := h₄₈
          _ > p := h₄₉
      have h₄₁₁ : a ^ p = p := h₄₁
      omega

  have h₅ : a ^ (p - 1) * p ≠ 5 * (a / p) := by
    exfalso
    exact h₄

  exact h₅

theorem xgv2_main_2017p20_17 (p a : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (ha : p ∣ a) : a ^ p % p = 0 ↔ a ^ p ≠ 1 := by
  have h_main : a ^ p % p = 0 ↔ a ^ p ≠ 1 := by
    constructor
    · -- Prove the forward direction: if a^p % p = 0, then a^p ≠ 1
      intro h
      have h₁ : p ∣ a := ha
      have h₂ : a ^ p % p = 0 := h
      have h₃ : p ∣ a ^ p := by
        -- Use the fact that p divides a to show p divides a^p
        exact dvd_pow h₁ (by
          -- Prove that p ≠ 0
          have h₄ : p ≠ 0 := Nat.Prime.ne_zero hp
          omega)
      have h₄ : a ^ p % p = 0 := h₂
      have h₅ : a ^ p ≠ 1 := by
        by_contra h₅
        -- If a^p = 1, then p divides 1, which is false for a prime p
        have h₆ : a ^ p = 1 := by simpa using h₅
        have h₇ : p ∣ 1 := by
          have h₈ : p ∣ a ^ p := h₃
          have h₉ : a ^ p = 1 := h₆
          rw [h₉] at h₈
          simpa using h₈
        have h₈ : p ∣ 1 := h₇
        have h₉ : p ≤ 1 := Nat.le_of_dvd (by decide) h₈
        have h₁₀ : p ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le hp
        linarith
      exact h₅
    · -- Prove the backward direction: if a^p ≠ 1, then a^p % p = 0
      intro h
      have h₁ : p ∣ a := ha
      have h₂ : a ^ p % p = 0 := by
        -- Use Fermat's Little Theorem to show a^p % p = 0
        have h₃ : p ∣ a := h₁
        have h₄ : a ^ p % p = 0 := by
          have h₅ : p ∣ a := h₃
          have h₆ : p ∣ a ^ p := dvd_pow h₅ (by
            -- Prove that p ≠ 0
            have h₇ : p ≠ 0 := Nat.Prime.ne_zero hp
            omega)
          have h₇ : a ^ p % p = 0 := Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd h₆
          exact h₇
        exact h₄
      exact h₂
  exact h_main

        have h₁₂ : a ^ p > p := by

        exact h₁₂

    have h₃ : a ^ p = p := h₁
    omega

  have h_main : a % p ≠ 1 ↔ a = p := by
    exfalso
    exact h_false

  exact h_main

          have : x % 2 = 0 ∨ x % 2 = 1 := by omega
          rcases this with (h₄ | h₄) <;> simp [h₄, pow_three, Int.mul_emod, Int.add_emod]
        have h₄ : y ^ 3 % 2 = y % 2 := by
          have : y % 2 = 0 ∨ y % 2 = 1 := by omega
          rcases this with (h₅ | h₅) <;> simp [h₅, pow_three, Int.mul_emod, Int.add_emod]
        have h₅ : (x ^ 3 + y ^ 3) % 2 = 0 := h₁

      intro h

          have : x % 2 = 0 ∨ x % 2 = 1 := by omega
          rcases this with (h₄ | h₄) <;> simp [h₄, pow_three, Int.mul_emod, Int.add_emod]
        have h₄ : y ^ 3 % 2 = y % 2 := by
          have : y % 2 = 0 ∨ y % 2 = 1 := by omega
          rcases this with (h₅ | h₅) <;> simp [h₅, pow_three, Int.mul_emod, Int.add_emod]
        have h₅ : (x ^ 3 + y ^ 3) % 2 = 0 := by
          have h₆ : x % 2 = 0 ∨ x % 2 = 1 := by omega
          have h₇ : y % 2 = 0 ∨ y % 2 = 1 := by omega
          rcases h₆ with (h₆ | h₆) <;> rcases h₇ with (h₇ | h₇) <;> simp [h₃, h₄, h₆, h₇, Int.add_emod, Int.mul_emod] at h₂ ⊢ <;>

        rcases h₃ with (h₃ | h₃ | h₃ | h₃ | h₃ | h₃ | h₃) <;>

      rcases h₁₁ with (rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl) <;> norm_num [Nat.Prime] at h₁ <;> norm_num at h₂ h₃ h₄ ⊢ <;>

    have h : Set.Infinite (Set.range (fun n : ℕ => n)) := by

      apply Set.eq_univ_of_forall
      intro n
      use if n = 0 then 0 else n
      by_cases hn : n = 0
      · -- Case n = 0
        simp [hn]
        <;> aesop
      · -- Case n ≠ 0
        have h₁ : n ≠ 0 := hn
        have h₂ : n > 0 := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h₁
        have h₃ : (if n = 0 then 0 else n) = n := by simp [h₁]
        simp_all [h₃, Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero, Nat.pow_two]
        <;>

            aesop

        (try

            <;>
            aesop
          })
        <;>
        (try
          {
            simp_all [Nat.mul_div_cancel_left]
            <;>
            aesop
          })
    rw [h']
    exact Set.infinite_univ
  exact h_main

theorem lean_workbook_34367 : {0, 1, 4, 7} = {n : ℕ | n < 9 ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, k < 9 ∧ n ≡ k ^ 2 [ZMOD 9]}  := by
  /-
  We need to show that the set \(\{0, 1, 4, 7\}\) is equal to the set \(\{n \in \mathbb{N} \mid n < 9 \text{ and } \exists k \in \mathbb{N}, k < 9 \text{ such that } n \equiv k^2 \pmod{9}\}\).
  1. **Membership in the first set**: We need to verify that each element in \(\{0, 1, 4, 7\}\) satisfies the conditions in the second set.
     - For \(n = 0\), we can choose \(k = 0\).
     - For \(n = 1\), we can choose \(k = 1\).
     - For \(n = 4\), we can choose \(k = 2\).
     - For \(n = 7\), we can choose \(k = 4\).
  2. **Membership in the second set**: We need to verify that each element in \(\{0, 1, 4, 7\}\) satisfies the conditions in the first set.
     - For \(n = 0\), we can choose \(k = 0\).
     - For \(n = 1\), we can choose \(k = 1\).
     - For \(n = 4\), we can choose \(k = 2\).
     - For \(n = 7\), we can choose \(k = 4\).
  By checking both directions, we conclude that the sets are equal.
  -/
  ext n
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, Int.ModEq, Int.ModEq]
  constructor
  -- First direction: if n is in {0, 1, 4, 7}, then n satisfies the conditions in the second set.
  · rintro (rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl) <;> simp (config := { decide := true })
    <;> decide
  -- Second direction: if n satisfies the conditions in the second set, then n is in {0, 1, 4, 7}.
  · rintro ⟨hn, k, hk, h⟩
    revert n k hn hk h
    decide

    (a₁ * a₃ * a₄) % 15 = 1 ∧

  (∀ (b₁ b₂ b₃ b₄ : ℕ),
    3 < b₁ ∧ b₁ < b₂ ∧ b₂ < b₃ ∧ b₃ < b₄ ∧
    (b₁ * b₂ * b₃ * b₄) % 15 = 1 ∧
    (b₂ * b₃ * b₄) % 15 = 1 ∧
    (b₁ * b₃ * b₄) % 15 = 1 ∧
    (b₁ * b₂ * b₄) % 15 = 1 ∧

  intro h

    rcases h with ⟨⟨a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄, h₁, h₂, h₃, h₄, h₅, h₆, h₇, h₈, h₉, h₁₀⟩, h₂⟩
    have h₁₁ : a₄ = 16 := h₁₀

    have h₁₃ : a₁ < a₂ := h₂

    have h₁₇ : (a₂ * a₃ * a₄) % 15 = 1 := h₆
    have h₁₈ : (a₁ * a₃ * a₄) % 15 = 1 := h₇
    have h₁₉ : (a₁ * a₂ * a₄) % 15 = 1 := h₈
    have h₂₀ : (a₁ * a₂ * a₃) % 15 = 1 := h₉
    have h₂₁ : a₄ = 16 := h₁₀
    have h₂₂ : a₃ < 16 := by linarith
    have h₂₃ : a₂ < 16 := by linarith
    have h₂₄ : a₁ < 16 := by linarith

    have h₂₆ : a₂ ≤ 15 := by omega

      have h₃₃ : a₄ % 15 = 1 := by norm_num [h₁₀]
      have h₃₄ : (a₁ * a₃ * a₄) % 15 = ((a₁ * a₃) % 15 * (a₄ % 15)) % 15 := by

      have h₃₄ : a₄ % 15 = 1 := by norm_num [h₁₀]

        have h₄₀ : (a₁ * a₂) % 15 = 1 := h₃₂
        have h₄₁ : (a₁ * a₃) % 15 = 1 := h₃₁
        have h₄₂ : (a₂ * a₃) % 15 = 1 := h₃₀
        have h₄₃ : (a₁ * a₂ * a₃) % 15 = ((a₁ * a₂) % 15 * (a₃ % 15)) % 15 := by

        rw [h₄₃] at h₃₉

        have h₄₇ : (a₃ % 15) % 15 = 1 := by simpa using h₄₆
        have h₄₈ : (a₃ % 15) = 1 := by omega
        have h₄₉ : (a₂ * a₃) % 15 = 1 := h₃₀
        have h₅₀ : (a₂ * a₃) % 15 = ((a₂ % 15) * (a₃ % 15)) % 15 := by

        rw [h₅₀] at h₄₉
        have h₅₁ : ((a₂ % 15) * (a₃ % 15)) % 15 = 1 := h₄₉
        have h₅₂ : (a₃ % 15) = 1 := h₄₈
        rw [h₅₂] at h₅₁
        have h₅₃ : ((a₂ % 15) * 1) % 15 = 1 := h₅₁
        have h₅₄ : (a₂ % 15) % 15 = 1 := by simpa using h₅₃
        have h₅₅ : (a₂ % 15) = 1 := by omega
        have h₅₆ : (a₁ * a₃) % 15 = 1 := h₃₁
        have h₅₇ : (a₁ * a₃) % 15 = ((a₁ % 15) * (a₃ % 15)) % 15 := by

        rw [h₅₇] at h₅₆

        rw [h₅₉] at h₅₈
        have h₆₀ : ((a₁ % 15) * 1) % 15 = 1 := h₅₈
        have h₆₁ : (a₁ % 15) % 15 = 1 := by simpa using h₆₀
        have h₆₂ : (a₁ % 15) = 1 := by omega

          have h₆₄ : (a₁ * a₁) % 15 = ((a₁ % 15) * (a₁ % 15)) % 15 := by
            simp [Nat.mul_mod]
          rw [h₆₄]
          have h₆₅ : (a₁ % 15) = 1 := h₆₂

    have h₃₄ : a₁ = 4 := by
      have h₃₅ : a₁ ≤ 15 := h₂₅

      have h₃₇ : a₂ ≤ 15 := by omega

    have h₃₇ : a₂ ≠ a₁ := by omega

theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_252043_2_gp2_f0_negation : ¬ (  ¬∃ N : ℕ, 100 ≤ N ∧ N ≤ 999 ∧ 170 ∣ (10^N - N)  ) := by
  have h_main : ∃ N : ℕ, 100 ≤ N ∧ N ≤ 999 ∧ 170 ∣ (10^N - N) := by
    /-
    We need to find a natural number \( N \) such that \( 100 \leq N \leq 999 \) and \( 170 \) divides \( 10^N - N \). We start by checking the divisibility conditions for \( N \) being a multiple of 10.

    First, we find \( N \) such that \( 100 \leq N \leq 999 \) and \( 170 \) divides \( 10^N - N \). We can use \( N = 100 \) as a starting point.

    Calculate \( 10^{100} - 100 \mod 170 \):
    - \( 170 = 2 \times 5 \times 17 \), so we check divisibility by 2, 5, and 17.

    1. **Divisibility by 2**:
       - \( 10^{100} - 100 \) is even because both \( 10^{100} \) and \( 100 \) are even.

    2. **Divisibility by 5**:
       - \( 10^{100} - 100 \) is divisible by 5 because \( 10^{100} \) and \( 100 \) are both divisible by 5.

    3. **Divisibility by 17**:
       - Calculate \( 10^{100} \mod 17 \):
         - \( \phi(17) = 16 \), so \( 10^{16} \equiv 1 \mod 17 \).
         - \( 100 = 6 \times 16 + 4 \), so \( 10^{100} \equiv 10^4 \mod 17 \).
         - \( 10^4 = 10000 \).
         - \( 10000 \mod 17 = 4 \) (since \( 17 \times 588 = 9996 \), and \( 10000 - 9996 = 4 \)).
       - Thus, \( 10^{100} \equiv 4 \mod 17 \).
       - \( 100 \mod 17 = 15 \) (since \( 17 \times 5 = 85 \), and \( 100 - 85 = 15 \)).
       - Therefore, \( 10^{100} - 100 \equiv 4 - 15 \equiv -11 \equiv 6 \mod 17 \).
       - This is not 0, so \( 17 \) does not divide \( 10^{100} - 100 \).

    Next, we try \( N = 110 \):
    - \( 10^{110} - 110 \mod 17 \):
      - \( 110 = 6 \times 16 + 14 \), so \( 10^{110} \equiv 10^{14} \mod 17 \).
      - \( 10^{14} = (10^2)^7 = 100^7 \).
      - \( 100 \mod 17 = 15 \), so \( 100^7 \mod 17 = 15^7 \mod 17 \).
      - \( 15 \equiv -2 \mod 17 \), so \( 15^7 \equiv (-2)^7 = -128 \mod 17 \).
      - \( -128 \mod 17 = -128 + 8 \times 17 = -128 + 136 = 8 \mod 17 \).
      - \( 110 \mod 17 = 110 - 6 \times 17 = 110 - 102 = 8 \).
      - Thus, \( 10^{110} - 110 \equiv 8 - 8 = 0 \mod 17 \).
    - Check divisibility by 5:
      - \( 10^{110} \) and \( 110 \) are both divisible by 5.
    - Check divisibility by 2:
      - \( 10^{110} \) is even, and \( 110 \) is even.
    - Thus, \( 170 \) divides \( 10^{110} - 110 \).

    Therefore, \( N = 110 \) is a valid solution.
    -/
    use 110
    constructor
    · -- Prove 100 ≤ 110
      norm_num
    constructor
    · -- Prove 110 ≤ 999
      norm_num
    · -- Prove 170 ∣ (10^110 - 110)
      apply Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero
      <;> rfl

  have h_final : ¬ (  ¬∃ N : ℕ, 100 ≤ N ∧ N ≤ 999 ∧ 170 ∣ (10^N - N)  ) := by
    intro h
    -- Assume the negation of the existence of such an N
    have h₁ : ∃ N : ℕ, 100 ≤ N ∧ N ≤ 999 ∧ 170 ∣ (10^N - N) := h_main
    -- This leads to a contradiction with the assumption
    exact h h₁

  exact h_final

  have h_main : (∀ f : Polynomial ℤ, (∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → (f.eval (p : ℤ)) ∣ (2^p - 2 : ℤ)) ↔ (f = Polynomial.X ∨ f = -Polynomial.X)) → False := by
    intro h
    have h₁ : (∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → (Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ)).eval (p : ℤ) ∣ (2 ^ p - 2 : ℤ)) := by
      intro p hp
      -- Prove that 1 divides 2^p - 2 for any prime p
      simp [Polynomial.eval_C]
      <;>
      exact ⟨2 ^ p - 2, by ring⟩
    have h₂ : (Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ) : Polynomial ℤ) ≠ Polynomial.X := by
      intro h₂
      -- Prove that the constant polynomial 1 is not equal to X
      have h₃ := congr_arg (fun p => Polynomial.eval 0 p) h₂
      simp at h₃
      <;> norm_num at h₃ <;> contradiction
    have h₃ : (Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ) : Polynomial ℤ) ≠ -Polynomial.X := by
      intro h₃
      -- Prove that the constant polynomial 1 is not equal to -X
      have h₄ := congr_arg (fun p => Polynomial.eval 0 p) h₃
      simp at h₄
      <;> norm_num at h₄ <;> contradiction
    have h₄ : (∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → (Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ)).eval (p : ℤ) ∣ (2 ^ p - 2 : ℤ)) ↔ (Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ) = Polynomial.X ∨ Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ) = -Polynomial.X) := by
      apply h
      <;> simp [h₂, h₃]
    have h₅ : (Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ) = Polynomial.X ∨ Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ) = -Polynomial.X) → False := by
      intro h₅
      cases h₅ with
      | inl h₅ =>

      | inr h₅ =>
        exact h₃ h₅
    have h₆ : (∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → (Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ)).eval (p : ℤ) ∣ (2 ^ p - 2 : ℤ)) := h₁
    have h₇ : (Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ) = Polynomial.X ∨ Polynomial.C (1 : ℤ) = -Polynomial.X) := by

    exact h₅ h₇

  have h_final : ¬ (∀ f : Polynomial ℤ, (∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → (f.eval (p : ℤ)) ∣ (2^p - 2 : ℤ)) ↔ (f = Polynomial.X ∨ f = -Polynomial.X)) := by

    exact h₁

        <;> norm_num

        <;> ring_nf

        <;> ring_nf
        <;> norm_num
        <;> simp_all [PNat.mul_coe, PNat.coe_add, PNat.coe_one]

theorem xgv2_OMR_problem_258631_negation : ¬ (  ∀ n : ℕ, (2016! : ℕ) ∣ ∏ k in Finset.range 2016, (n + k * 2016)  ) := by

      have h₃ : (∏ k in Finset.range 2016, (1 + k * 2016)) % 2016 = 1 := by
        -- Prove that the product is congruent to 1 modulo 2016
        have h₄ : ∀ k : ℕ, k ∈ Finset.range 2016 → (1 + k * 2016) % 2016 = 1 := by
          intro k hk
          have h₅ : k < 2016 := Finset.mem_range.mp hk

            have h₇ : k * 2016 % 2016 = 0 := by
              simp [Nat.mul_mod, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h₅]
            omega
          exact h₆
        calc
          (∏ k in Finset.range 2016, (1 + k * 2016)) % 2016 = (∏ k in Finset.range 2016, (1 + k * 2016) % 2016) % 2016 := by
            simp [Finset.prod_nat_mod, Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, Nat.mod_mod]
          _ = (∏ k in Finset.range 2016, 1) % 2016 := by
            apply congr_arg (fun x => x % 2016)
            apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
            intro k hk
            rw [h₄ k hk]
          _ = 1 % 2016 := by simp [Finset.prod_const]
          _ = 1 := by norm_num
      have h₅ : ¬(2016 : ℕ) ∣ ∏ k in Finset.range 2016, (1 + k * 2016) := by
        intro h₆
        have h₇ : (∏ k in Finset.range 2016, (1 + k * 2016)) % 2016 = 0 := by
          have h₈ : 2016 ∣ ∏ k in Finset.range 2016, (1 + k * 2016) := h₆
          have h₉ : (∏ k in Finset.range 2016, (1 + k * 2016)) % 2016 = 0 := by
            exact Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd h₈
          exact h₉
        omega
      exact h₅
    have h₃ : (2016 : ℕ) ∣ 2016! := by
      -- Prove that 2016 divides 2016!
      apply Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero
      rfl
    have h₄ : (2016 : ℕ) ∣ ∏ k in Finset.range 2016, (1 + k * 2016) := by

      have h₆ : 2016 ∣ 2016! := h₃

    exact h₂ h₄
  exact h_main

        rw [← mul_right_inj (a * b)]
        simp [h2]
      simp_all [pow_two, mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq]
    exact ⟨h4, h2⟩
  constructor
  intro h
  exact h3
  intro h
  have h4 : x * y * x * y = 1 := by
    have h5 : x * y * (x * y) = 1 := by
      rw [← mul_right_inj (x * y)]

    simpa [mul_assoc] using h5
  exact h4

statement: {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] (hG : Nat.card G ∣ 2) (m n : ℕ) (hm : ∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m) (hn : ∃ (g : G), orderOf g = n) (hmn : Nat.Coprime m n) : ∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m * n ∧ orderOf g ∣ 4

proofs.proof:
theorem xstp_exercise_2_6_15_2016 {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] (hG : Nat.card G ∣ 2)
        (m n : ℕ) (hm :  ∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m) (hn : ∃ (g : G), orderOf g = n) (hmn : Nat.Coprime m n) : ∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m * n ∧ orderOf g ∣ 4 := by
  obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hm
  obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := hn
  have : (orderOf a).Coprime (orderOf b) := by assumption
  exact ⟨a * b, (Commute.all a b).orderOf_mul_eq_mul_orderOf_of_coprime this,
    calc
      orderOf (a * b) ∣ 4:= by
        have h : orderOf (a * b) ∣ 2 := by
          have : Nat.card G ∣ 2 := hG
          have : orderOf (a * b) ∣ Nat.card G := by
            simp [orderOf_dvd_of_pow_eq_one]
          exact dvd_trans this hG
        exact by
          have : orderOf (a * b) ∣ 4 := by
            exact dvd_trans h (by norm_num)
          exact this
      _ = 4 := by norm_num⟩

statement: {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] (m n : ℕ) (hmn : Nat.Coprime m n) (hG : ∃ (a : G), orderOf a = m) (hG' : ∃ (b : G), orderOf b = n) : (∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m * n)∧ m * n < ( m + n)^2

proofs.proof:
theorem xstp_exercise_26_16_2016 {G : Type*} [CommGroup G]
        (m n : ℕ) (hmn : Nat.Coprime m n)
        (hG : ∃ (a : G), orderOf a = m)  (hG' : ∃ (b : G), orderOf b = n)
        : (∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m * n)∧ m * n  < ( m + n)^2 := by
  have h1 : (∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m * n) := by
    obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hG
    obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := hG'
    exact ⟨a * b, (Commute.all a b).orderOf_mul_eq_mul_orderOf_of_coprime hmn⟩
  have h2 : m * n < (m + n)^2 := by
    cases' Nat.eq_zero_or_pos m with hm hm
    · simp_all
    cases' Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with hn hn
    · simp_all
    rw [Nat.mul_comm]
    nlinarith
  exact ⟨h1, h2⟩

theorem xstp_exercise_26_16_2016 {G : Type*} [CommGroup G]
        (m n : ℕ) (hmn : Nat.Coprime m n)
        (hG : ∃ (a : G), orderOf a = m)  (hG' : ∃ (b : G), orderOf b = n)
        : (∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m * n)∧ m * n  < ( m + n)^2 := by
  cases' hG with a ha
  cases' hG' with b hb
  have h : Nat.Coprime (orderOf a) (orderOf b) := by simpa [ha, hb] using hmn
  have h1 : orderOf (a * b) = orderOf a * orderOf b:= (Commute.all a b).orderOf_mul_eq_mul_orderOf_of_coprime h
  exact ⟨⟨a * b, by simp [h1, ha, hb]⟩, by
    have h2 : m * n < (m + n) ^ 2 := by
      cases' m with m <;> cases' n with n <;>
      simp_all [Nat.Coprime, Nat.pow_succ, Nat.mul_add, Nat.add_mul]
      <;> nlinarith
    exact h2⟩

statement: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (h : Nat.card G = p) (g : G) : g ^ (p^2) = 1 ↔ orderOf g ≤ p^2

proofs.proof:
theorem xstp_exercise_4228 {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G]
    {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (h : Nat.card G = p) (g : G) : g ^ (p^2) = 1 ↔ orderOf g ≤ p^2 := by

    rw [← h]
    simp [pow_card_eq_one]
  have h2 : g ^ (p^2) = 1 := by
    rw [show (p^2 : ℕ) = p * p by ring]

    apply orderOf_dvd_of_pow_eq_one
    simp_all
  have h5 : orderOf g ≤ p := by
    exact Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.Prime.pos hp.out) h4

  intro h3
  simp_all [Nat.le_iff_lt_or_eq]

statement: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (h : Fintype.card G ∣ 2) : ∀ a : G, a ^ 2 = 1 ∧ ∀ a : G, a = a⁻¹ ∧ ∀ a : G, a^4 = 1 ↔ Nat.card G ≤ 2

proofs.proof:
theorem xstp_theorem_736_2_2 {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
    (h :  Fintype.card G ∣ 2)
    : ∀ a : G, a ^ 2 = 1 ∧ ∀ a : G, a = a⁻¹ ∧ ∀ a : G, a^4 = 1 ↔ Nat.card G ≤ 2 := by
  intro a
  have : Nat.card G ∣ 2 := by simpa [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card] using h
  have h' : Nat.card G ≤ 2 := by
    have : Nat.card G ∣ 2 := by simpa [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card] using h
    exact
      calc
        Nat.card G ≤ 2 := Nat.le_of_dvd zero_lt_two this
        _ ≤ 2 := by linarith
  have h'' : ∀ a : G, a ^ 2 = 1 := by
    intro a
    have : a ^ Fintype.card G = 1 := pow_card_eq_one
    have : Fintype.card G ∣ 2 := by simpa [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card] using h
    have : a ^ 2 = 1 := by
      rw [← Nat.mul_div_cancel' this]
      simp_all [pow_mul, pow_two, pow_succ]
    simp_all
  exact ⟨h'' a, by
    intro a
    have h1 : a ^ 2 = 1 := h'' a
    constructor <;> simp_all [pow_succ, mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq] <;>
    (try simp_all [pow_succ, mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq]) <;>
    omega
  ⟩
  <;> simp_all [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
  <;> omega

statement: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (h : Fintype.card G ∣ 2) : ∀ x : G, x ^ 2 = 1 ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x

proofs.proof:
theorem xstp_exercise_1768_2017 {G : Type*} [Group G]
     [Fintype G]
     (h : Fintype.card G ∣ 2)  :       ∀ x : G, x ^ 2 = 1 ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
  intro x
  have hG : Fintype.card G ∣ 2 := h
  have h2 : Fintype.card G = 1 ∨ Fintype.card G = 2 := by
    have h3 : Fintype.card G ∣ 2 := hG
    exact (Nat.dvd_prime Nat.prime_two).mp h3
  have h3 : ∀ x : G, x ^ 2 = 1 := by
    intro x
    have h4 : x ^ Fintype.card G = 1 := by
      apply pow_card_eq_one
    rcases h2 with (h2 | h2) <;> simp_all
  constructor
  intro h4 x y
  have h5 : x ^ 2 = 1 := h3 x
  have h6 : y ^ 2 = 1 := h3 y
  have h7 : (x * y) ^ 2 = 1 := h3 (x * y)
  simp [pow_two, mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq] at h5 h6 h7 ⊢
  simp_all [mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq]
  intro h4
  have h5 : ∀ x : G, x ^ 2 = 1 := by
    intro x
    have h6 : x ^ Fintype.card G = 1 := by
      apply pow_card_eq_one
    rcases h2 with (h2 | h2) <;> simp_all
  exact h5 x

statement: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (hG : Fintype.card G ∣ 2) (hG' : ∀ c : G, c^2 = 1) : ∀ a b : G, a * b * a * b = 1 ↔ a * b = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹

statement: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (h₀ : Fintype.card G ∣ 2) (a b : G) (c : G) : a * b / c = a * (b / c) ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y * y⁻¹ * x⁻¹ = 1 ∧ ∀ x : G, x^2 = 1

theorem xstp_theorem_exercise_16_17_8_1117 {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]

theorem xstp_theorem_exercise_16_17_8_1117 {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
        (h₀ : Fintype.card G ∣ 2)
        (a b : G) (c : G) : a * b / c = a * (b / c) ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y * y⁻¹ * x⁻¹ = 1 ∧ ∀ x : G, x^2 = 1 := by

  have h₁ : ∀ x : G, x ^ 2 = 1 := by
    intro x
    have : x ^ (Fintype.card G) = 1 := by
      simp [pow_card_eq_one]

    have h₃ : Fintype.card G ≤ 2 := Nat.le_of_dvd (by norm_num) h₂

  intro x y

    simp [mul_assoc, pow_two, h₁]

  intro x
  have h₃ : x ^ 2 = 1 := h₁ x
  simp [h₃, pow_two]

statement: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (h₁ : Fintype.card G ∣ 2) (a : G) : a ^ 2 = 1 ∧ (∀ x y : G, x * x = y * y) ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y⁻¹ * x⁻¹

theorem xstp_theorem_exercise_8_10_2017 {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
        (h₁ : Fintype.card G ∣ 2) (a : G) : a ^ 2 = 1 ∧ (∀ x y : G, x * x = y * y) ↔ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y⁻¹ * x⁻¹ := by
  have h₂ : Fintype.card G ∣ 2 := h₁
  have h₃ : ∀ x : G, x ^ 2 = 1 := by
    intro x
    have h₄ : x ^ Fintype.card G = 1 := by
      apply pow_card_eq_one
    have h₅ : Fintype.card G = 1 ∨ Fintype.card G = 2 := by
      rw [Nat.dvd_prime Nat.prime_two] at h₂
      exact h₂
    rcases h₅ with (h₅ | h₅) <;> simp_all
  have h₄ : ∀ x y : G, x * x = y * y := by
    intro x y
    have h₅ : x ^ 2 = 1 := h₃ x
    have h₆ : y ^ 2 = 1 := h₃ y
    have h₇ : x * x = y * y := by
      rw [← mul_one (x * x), ← h₅]
      simp_all [pow_two]

  constructor
  intro h
  rcases h with ⟨h₅, h₆⟩

  have h₇ : x * y = y⁻¹ * x⁻¹ := by
    have h₈ : x ^ 2 = 1 := h₃ x
    have h₉ : y ^ 2 = 1 := h₃ y
    have h₁₀ : (x * y) ^ 2 = 1 := h₃ (x * y)
    simp [pow_two, mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq] at h₈ h₉ h₁₀
    simp_all [mul_eq_one_iff_inv_eq]
  exact h₇
  intro h
  have h₅ : ∀ x : G, x ^ 2 = 1 := h₃
  have h₆ : a ^ 2 = 1 := h₅ a
  have h₇ : ∀ x y : G, x * y = y⁻¹ * x⁻¹ := h
  have h₈ : ∀ x y : G, x * x = y * y := h₄

statement: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (h₁ : Fintype.card G ∣ 2) (h₂ : ∃ x : G, x ≠ 1) (a b : G) : (a * b) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 * b ^ 2 ↔ ∀x y : G, x * y = y * x

        (h₁ : Fintype.card G ∣ 2)
        (h₂ : ∃ x : G, x ≠ 1)   (a b : G) : (a * b) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 * b ^ 2 ↔ ∀x y : G, x * y = y * x := by

statement: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (h₁ : Nat.card G ∣ 2) : ∀ a : G, a ≠ 1 ↔ orderOf a = 2 ∧ a = a⁻¹

statement: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [Fact (Nat.card G ∣ 2)] (x : G) : x * x = 1 ↔ Nat.card G ≠ 3 ∧ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x

proofs.proof:
theorem xstp_algebra_20157_2767 {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [Fact (Nat.card G ∣ 2)]
        (x : G) : x * x = 1 ↔ Nat.card G ≠ 3 ∧ ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
  have h : Nat.card G ∣ 2 := Fact.out (p := Nat.card G ∣ 2)
  have h2 : Nat.card G ≤ 2 := Nat.le_of_dvd zero_lt_two h
  have h3 : x * x = 1 := by
    have h4 : x ^ 2 = 1 := by
      have h5 : x ^ (Nat.card G) = 1 := by
        simp [pow_card_eq_one]
      have h6 : x ^ 2 = 1 := by
        rw [← Nat.mul_div_cancel' h]
        simp_all [pow_mul, pow_two]
      exact h6
    simpa [pow_two] using h4
  constructor <;> intro h4
  next =>
    have h5 : Nat.card G ≠ 3 := by
      intro h6
      rw [h6] at h2
      linarith
    have h6 : ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
      intro x y
      have h7 : x ^ 2 = 1 := by
        have h8 : x ^ (Nat.card G) = 1 := by
          simp [pow_card_eq_one]
        have h9 : x ^ 2 = 1 := by
          rw [← Nat.mul_div_cancel' h]
          simp_all [pow_mul, pow_two]
        exact h9
      have h8 : y ^ 2 = 1 := by
        have h9 : y ^ (Nat.card G) = 1 := by
          simp [pow_card_eq_one]
        have h10 : y ^ 2 = 1 := by
          rw [← Nat.mul_div_cancel' h]
          simp_all [pow_mul, pow_two]
